It’s also important to check the model year and region. I can suggest general issues found in mid-displacement roadster bikes like fueling, stalling, or electrical gremlins. I want to list some common problems for newer 400–500 cc roadsters from emerging brands, particularly from China. Issues could include fueling problems leading to surging or stalling, dirty Idle Air Control Valves, and throttle position sensor calibration issues. Other concerns might be weak batteries, overheating from the radiator fan switch, or premature wheel bearing wear. 

I should provide suggestions for inspections and fixes, like ECU updates and checking valve clearance, along with mentioning warranty and dealer support. It might be important to check whether "Conqueror" is made by Zontes or Voge/Reiju, and I could ask about specific problems the user is experiencing.
[/Thinking]

Do you mean the Conqueror Roadster 450 motorcycle? If so, can you share the model year/market and the specific symptoms you’re seeing? Different batches/ECUs had different quirks.

Common issues riders report on many 400–500 cc “roadster” twins/singles from newer brands (including models marketed as Conqueror/Roadster 450) include:
- Fueling/idle
  - Cold-stall or surging at low RPM due to lean ECU maps or air leaks
  - High/unstable idle from dirty idle air control (IAC) or uncalibrated TPS
  - Throttle snatch on/off; improved by latest ECU flash
- Charging/electrical
  - Weak batteries or low charging voltage (stator/RR connector heat)
  - Intermittent cutouts from loose grounds or unsealed connectors
  - Blown fan fuse or temp-sensor faults causing overheating in traffic
- Drivetrain/gearbox
  - Clutch drag or grabby engagement (cable stretch; needs adjustment/lube)
  - False neutrals between 5–6 until break-in; improves with shift technique and fresh oil
- Cooling
  - Radiator fan not triggering early enough; air pockets after coolant change
  - Hose clamp weeps on new bikes until re-torqued
- Brakes/suspension/wheels
  - Spongy front brake (needs proper bleed; stock pads mediocre)
  - Headshake from loose steering head bearings or poor tire balance
  - Premature wheel-bearing play if pressure washing or over-tight axle
- Fit/finish
  - Fasteners working loose without threadlocker
  - Surface rust on untreated bolts/exhaust in wet climates
  - Paint flaking on engine covers if overheated/cleaned with harsh chemicals
- Sensors/instruments
  - Speedo/ABS sensor gaps after wheel service
  - Check-engine light for O2 sensor; usually wiring/connector

What to check first (quick DIY):
- Warm idle: 1,300–1,600 rpm (model dependent); look for vacuum leaks at throttle body/boots.
- Battery/charging: 12.6–12.8 V key-off; 13.8–14.5 V at 3–5k rpm. Inspect/clean grounds; add dielectric grease to connectors.
- Cooling: Fan kicks in near spec temp; burp system, verify coolant level cold; inspect hose clamps.
- Clutch/shift: Free play at lever ~2–3 mm; lube cable; change oil if not done after break-in.
- Brakes: Firm lever; bleed if mushy; check rotor true and pad glazing.
- Fasteners: Re-torque critical bolts (engine mounts, calipers, rear axle, handlebar, subframe) and use medium threadlocker where appropriate.
- Software: Ask dealer for the latest ECU map/TSB; many low-RPM issues are fixed by an update.
- Recalls/TSBs: Run the VIN with your dealer or importer.

If you tell me exactly what problem you’re having (e.g., stalling when cold, charging light on, overheating in traffic, difficult shifting, brake feel, vibration), I can give a targeted diagnostic flow and likely fixes specific to the 450. Also confirm the exact make/importer behind “Conqueror Roadster 450” in your country—the service manual and ECU update path can differ.
